To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
oxime ligation of post-solid phase peptides can facilitate the discovery of new binding sites for protein-protein interaction antagonists.

oxime-based post-solid-phase peptide diversification can be applied to optimize the interactions of a high affinity peptide ligand of the Plk1 polo-box domain, resulting in up to a two orders of magnitude increase in binding affinity.

oxime-based post-SPS diversification of the Pro residue in the high affinity 5mer PLHSpT peptide allowed the discovery of new binding interactions that enhanced the affinity of the peptide for the polo-like kinase (Plk) polo-box domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of small molecule inhibitors of Plk1 PDB binding as potential anti-tumor agents.
the development of new inhibitors of the polo-like kinases (Plks), a family of mitotic kinases with important roles in cell cycle progression and tumor suppression.
the development of novel protein-protein interaction modulators for the polo-like kinase family, which are currently under investigation as potential anticancer therapeutics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxime ligation strategy is an effective tool for improving protein-protein interaction inhibitor design.
oxime-based post-SPS diversification of a 5-mer PBD ligand resulted in a 100-fold potency increase.
the oxime-based diversifying chemistry is a valuable tool for the identification and optimization of protein-protein interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oxime ligation of peptides can be an extremely useful tool for the discovery of new binding sites on target proteins.
we have identified a new binding pocket in the polo-box domain of Plk1 that is amenable to ligand binding and that can be targeted by small molecules.
the use of oxime chemistry in the development of protein ligands can lead to the identification of novel binding sites that can be further optimized for the development of potent inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oxime-based post-solid phase peptide diversification is a powerful strategy for identifying new binding interactions in protein-protein interfaces.

the oxime-based diversifications of amino acid residues can provide a powerful tool for the identification of high affinity ligands for protein-protein interaction surfaces that would otherwise not be accessible to natural amino acids.
oxime ligation of a post solid-phase peptide is a very effective strategy to improve the affinity of a high affinity peptide.
